newsitem.title: USA: SWIMMING-CARVIN RETURNS AFTER HEART PROBLEMS.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-CARVIN RETURNS AFTER HEART PROBLEMS.

text.p: Chad Carvin made a
successful return to swimming at the U.S. National Swimming
Championships on Friday.
Carvin, 22, American record holder in the 1,000-meter
freestyle, won the 200-meter freestyle in one minute, 50.42
seconds. He also won the 400-meter individual medley in
4:21.77. Only 45 minutes separated the races.
It was his sixth and seventh national titles in his first
major swim meet since the winter of 1995.
Carvin was ranked second in the world in 1996 in the 200-
and 400-meter freestyle events. He is a three-time national
and PAC-10 champion, two-time NCAA champion and 12-time
All-Ameri Though his senior year was cut short and his appeals to
remain eligible for college competition were turned down by
the NCAA, Carvin's Olympic hopes have been rekindled for for
Three months before the '96 Olympic Trials, Carvin, then
21, was diagnosed with cardiomyopathy, a low-grade virus that
attacks the heart muscles.
Carvin was told to stop training and rest for 90 days,
wiping out any chance of making the Olympic team. He was
favoured to make the team.
"I feel like I am the luckiest person alive," Carvin said.
The five-day national championship meet is his first
national swimming championship since being told that he may
never swim again.
"I was prepared to deal with it even if I couldn't come
back," Carvin said. "I am just happy everything worked out the
way it did. I feel reborn.
"Swimming has been such a big part of my life ... to have
it gone ... that was the most difficult thing. That was more
disappointing then not making the Olympic team. I just kept
asking myself 'what am I supposed to be doing now?'"
Frank Busch, Carvin's coach at University of Arizona, says
it's a miracle the Laguna Hills, Calif. native is still alive,
let alone swimming.
Doctors allowed Carvin, who had been sleeping 15 hours a
day, to resume light exercise last summer after discovering
the heart wall had repaired itself.
"Just walking around made me tired," Carvin said. "In the
early stages I didn't want to do anything. When I felt my
energy coming back, I had a feeling things were going well."
Carvin, though still under a doctor's care and required to
take heart medication for the rest of his life, has been
allowed to return to swimming and his other loves, mountain
biking and surfing.
"I'll never know whether I would have made the Olympic
team," Carvin said. "It was rough watching Olympic Trials on
TV but the Olympics got me motivated.
"If I were to finish 20th here, this would probably be my
last meet. But as long as I final and am competitive, I'll
know I'm back for good."
In other races Friday, two-time Olympian Jenny Thompson
won the 200-meter freestyle in a pool record 2:01.45. She won
the 100 freestyle title Thursday. It was the first major meet
since the Olympic Games, where Thompson won three gold medals
on relays.
Schoolgirl Jennifer Parmenter won the 400-meter individual
medley in 4:43.72.
The five-day long course meters meet ends Sunday.
